data.raw_text:
Tonight, President Donald Trump recognized a 99 year old World War II veteran of the Battle of Manila during the State of the Union.

In 1945, nearly 4,000 American and Allied civilians were being held in Manila at Santo Tomas and other locations.

From February 3 to March 3, 1945, U.S. forces fought one of the largest and most destructive urban battles in American military history.

More than 16,000 Japanese naval and army defenders were killed inside the city. The internees were liberated. Manila was freed.

The cost was staggering. Approximately 100,000 Filipino civilians were killed, many massacred by Japanese forces during the battle. Much of the city was destroyed.

General Douglas MacArthur initially restricted aerial bombing to preserve the city, but heavy ground combat and artillery fire turned Manila into one of the most devastated Allied cities of World War II.

Urban warfare has always been decisive, brutal, and tragic. Tonight we honored one of the men who fought it.
